hints.title: Initial Increasing Order with Segment Inversion
hints.text: Begin with natural numbers 1 through n + 1 in ascending order. Contiguous sequences of D indicate segments that must be reversed.

hints.title: Reversing Descending Runs Greedily
hints.text: Whenever a contiguous run of D appears from index i to j, reversing the corresponding values from index i to j + 1 produces the smallest lexicographical result.

hints.title: Two Pointer Segment Reversal
hints.text: Initialize res = list(range(1, len(s) + 2)). Iterate through s. When s[i] == D, track starting index, scan until next I or string end, and reverse res[start:end + 1].

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: length of pattern string s
complexity.notes: Optimal linear O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space inverting contiguous descending segments.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing permutations lexicographically until finding one that satisfies the pattern takes O(N!) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Greedy subarray reversal operates directly on the output permutation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should understand why reversing runs of D achieves the smallest lexicographical permutation.
